title: Russian forces seize the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
body:
Russian forces seized the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant on 4 March 2022, days after the full-scale invasion began, when an armoured column approached overnight and fighting broke out. A fire in a training facility was extinguished, a bullet pierced an outer wall of Reactor 4 and an artillery shell hit a transformer at Reactor 6. By 12 March the Russian state company Rosatom claimed control of the plant, although actual control of operations remained unclear for months.

The plant, in Enerhodar on the Dnipro, has six VVER-1000 reactors rated at 950 megawatts electric each, for a total of 5,700 megawatts. It is the largest nuclear power plant in Europe and was operated by Ukraine's Energoatom from 1996 until the occupation. In 2020 it produced nearly half of Ukraine's nuclear electricity, and about 1.3 gigawatts of capacity was lost when it was seized.

An International Atomic Energy Agency delegation visited the plant in early September 2022 and published a report on 6 September documenting damage and security threats from shelling and the presence of occupying troops. Of the plant's original four 750-kilovolt lines and one 330-kilovolt line, three of the 750-kilovolt lines have been destroyed. Since the plant was captured it has generated no power. Five units are generally kept in cold shutdown and one in hot shutdown. Since the Kakhovka Dam was destroyed in June 2023, cooling water has come from 11 groundwater wells, according to the Wikipedia article.
